units.zh: 資治通鑑第083卷
units.en: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 83
units.literal: Comprehensive Mirror to Aid in Government, Volume 83

units.zh: 【晉紀五】起屠維協洽，盡目章涒灘，凡二年。
units.en: [Jin Records 5] runs from the year gengwu through guisi, spanning two years in all.
units.literal: [Jin Records 5] beginning at gengwu, ending at guisi, altogether two years.

units.zh: 孝惠皇帝上之下元康九年（
units.en: Under Emperor Hui of Jin, Yuankang, year 9 (
units.literal: The lower portion of the first reign of Emperor Xiaohui, ninth year of Yuankang (

units.zh: 己未，公元二九九年）
units.en: jiwei, CE 299)
units.literal: jiwei, common era year 299)

units.zh: 春，正月，孟觀大破氐眾於中亭，獲齊萬年。
units.en: In spring, the first month, Meng Guan routed the Di forces at Zhongting and took Qi Wannian prisoner.
units.literal: In spring, the first month, Meng Guan greatly defeated the Di host at Zhongting and captured Qi Wannian.

units.zh: 太子洗馬陳留江統以為戎、狄亂華，宜早絕其原，乃作《徙戎論》以警朝廷曰：「夫夷、蠻、戎、狄，地在要荒，禹平九土而西戎即敘。
units.en: Jiang Tong of Chenliu, Groom of the Heir Apparent, argued that the Rong and Di were already unsettling the realm and that their root cause should be severed at once. He wrote the "Discourse on Relocating the Rong" to admonish the court, saying: "The Yi, Man, Rong, and Di inhabit the far marches. After Yu brought order to the nine domains, the western Rong at once came to allegiance.
units.literal: The Groom of the Heir Apparent, Jiang Tong of Chenliu, held that the Rong and Di were disturbing China and that their source ought to be cut off early; he therefore composed the "Discourse on Relocating the Rong" to warn the court, saying: "The Yi, Man, Rong, and Di dwell in the remote borderlands. When Yu pacified the nine regions, the western Rong forthwith submitted.

units.zh: 其性氣貪婪，凶悍不仁。
units.en: By nature they are greedy, brutal, and devoid of human feeling.
units.literal: Their nature and temperament are greedy, fierce, and lacking in humaneness.

units.zh: 四夷之中，戎、狄為甚，弱則畏服，強則侵叛。
units.en: Of the four barbarian peoples, the Rong and Di are the most troublesome: when weak they bow in awe, when strong they raid and revolt.
units.literal: Among the four Yi, the Rong and Di are the worst: when weak they fear and submit; when strong they invade and rebel.

units.zh: 當其強也，以漢之高祖困於白登，孝文軍於霸上；
units.en: When they grew strong, Han Gaozu was trapped at Baideng and Emperor Wen camped at Bashang;
units.literal: When they were strong, Gaozu of Han was besieged at Baideng and Emperor Xiaowen encamped at Bashang;

units.zh: 及其弱也，以元、成之微而單于入朝。
units.en: when they weakened, under the enfeebled reigns of Yuan and Cheng the Chanyu presented himself at court.
units.literal: when they grew weak, under the feebleness of Emperors Yuan and Cheng the Chanyu came to court.

units.zh: 此其已然之效也。
units.en: This is the pattern history has already shown.
units.literal: These are effects that have already come to pass.

units.zh: 是以有道之君牧夷、狄也，惟以待之有備，御之有常，雖稽顙執贄，而邊城不弛固守，強暴為寇，而兵甲不加遠征，期令境內獲安，疆場不侵而已。
units.en: That is why a ruler who holds to the Way deals with the Yi and Di by standing ready and governing them through steady discipline. Even when they prostrate themselves and bring tribute, frontier garrisons never slacken their guard; even when they turn violent and raid, no distant punitive expedition is launched—the goal is only domestic tranquility and an unmolested border.
units.literal: Therefore when a ruler possessed of the Way governs the Yi and Di, he only treats them with preparedness and controls them by constant measures: though they knock their foreheads and present tribute, the border cities do not relax their firm defense; though violence makes them raiders, arms and armor are not sent on distant campaigns—the aim is simply that the interior may gain peace and the frontier not be violated.

units.zh: 及至周室失統，諸侯專征，封疆不固，而利害異心，戎、狄乘間，得入中國，或招誘安撫以為己用，自是四夷交侵，與中國錯居。
units.en: But when the Zhou royal house lost control and the feudal lords fought wars on their own, borders ceased to hold and loyalties split. The Rong and Di seized the chance to enter the Central States, some lords even recruiting and appeasing them for private ends. From that point the four Yi pressed in from every side and lived mixed among the Chinese.
units.literal: When the Zhou house lost its mandate and the feudal lords waged war on their own authority, the frontiers were no longer secure and interests diverged in heart; the Rong and Di seized the opening and were able to enter China, some being recruited and placated for one's own use—from then on the four Yi invaded in turn and dwelt intermingled with China.

units.zh: 及秦始皇並天下，兵威旁達，攘胡走越，當是時，中國無復四夷也。
units.en: When the First Emperor of Qin united the empire and his armies reached to every quarter, he swept the Hu aside and drove the Yue away; for a time China was again free of the four Yi.
units.literal: When the First Emperor of Qin united the realm and military might reached in every direction, he drove off the Hu and put the Yue to flight; at that time China had no more of the four Yi.

units.zh: 漢建武中，馬援領隴西太守，討叛羌，徙其餘種於關中，居馮翊、河東空地。
units.en: Under Emperor Guangwu of Han, Ma Yuan served as Administrator of Longxi, put down rebellious Qiang bands, and moved the survivors into Guanzhong, placing them on empty land in Fufeng and Hedong.
units.literal: In the Jianwu era of Han, Ma Yuan held the post of Administrator of Longxi, suppressed the rebellious Qiang, and relocated the remnant clans into Guanzhong, settling them on vacant lands in Fufeng and Hedong.

units.zh: 數歲之後，族類蕃息，既恃其肥強，且苦漢人侵之；
units.en: Within a few years their numbers swelled. Trusting in their new strength and bitter over Han oppression,
units.literal: After several years the tribes multiplied; relying on their growing strength and resenting Han encroachment upon them,

units.zh: 永初之元，群羌叛亂，覆沒將守，屠破城邑，鄧騭敗北，侵及河內。
units.en: in the first year of Yongchu the Qiang rebelled en masse, wiping out commanders and garrisons and ravaging towns. Deng Sui suffered defeat in the north, and the turmoil reached Henei.
units.literal: in the first year of Yongchu the Qiang rose in rebellion, overthrowing generals and garrison commanders, slaughtering and destroying cities; Deng Sui was defeated in the north and the raids reached into Henei.

units.zh: 十年之中，夷、夏俱敝，任尚、馬賢，僅乃克之。
units.en: For ten years barbarian and Chinese alike were worn down; only Ren Shang and Ma Xian barely managed to suppress the uprising.
units.literal: Within ten years both Yi and Xia were exhausted; only Ren Shang and Ma Xian barely succeeded in subduing them.

units.zh: 自此之後，餘燼不盡，小有際會，輒復侵叛，中世之寇，惟此為大。
units.en: Afterward the embers were never fully stamped out; at the slightest chance they rebelled again. Among the calamities of the middle Han, none proved greater.
units.literal: From then on embers were never fully extinguished; at the slightest opportunity they again raided and rebelled—the scourge of the middle age, none greater than this.

units.zh: 魏興之初，與蜀分隔，疆場之戎，一彼一此。
units.en: When Wei first rose and was separated from Shu, the frontier Rong were likewise divided between the two realms.
units.literal: At the beginning of Wei's rise, when it was divided from Shu, the Rong of the frontier were split, some on one side and some on the other.

units.zh: 武帝徙武都氐於秦州，欲以弱寇強國，扞御蜀虜，此蓋權宜之計，非萬世之利也。
units.en: Emperor Wu of Jin moved the Di of Wudu into Qinzhou, hoping to weaken the enemy, strengthen the state, and block Shu. That was an expedient, not a policy that would profit all posterity.
units.literal: Emperor Wu relocated the Di of Wudu to Qinzhou, intending to weaken the foe and strengthen the state and to shield against the Shu enemy—this was only an expedient measure, not a benefit for ten thousand generations.

units.zh: 今者當之，已受其敝矣。
units.en: Today we are already paying the price.
units.literal: As for the present, we are already suffering its harm.

units.zh: 夫關中土沃物豐，帝王所居，未聞戎、狄宜在此土也。
units.en: Guanzhong is rich soil in a land of plenty, the seat of emperors and kings. No one has ever said the Rong and Di belong there.
units.literal: Guanzhong's soil is fertile and its goods abundant—the dwelling place of emperors and kings; one has never heard that the Rong and Di are suited to this land.

units.zh: 非我族類，其心必異。
units.en: They are not of our kind; their hearts cannot be the same as ours.
units.literal: Those who are not of our kind by birth will surely differ in heart.

units.zh: 而因其衰敝，遷之畿服，士庶玩習，侮其輕弱，使其怨恨之氣毒於骨髓；
units.en: Yet when they were weak we moved them into the heartland. Officials and commoners learned to treat them lightly and bully them, until hatred settled deep in their bones;
units.literal: Yet because they were in decline and weakness they were moved into the metropolitan domain; officials and commoners grew accustomed to trifling with them and insulting their feebleness, so that resentment sank poison into the marrow of their bones;

units.zh: 至於蕃育眾盛，則坐生其心。
units.en: and once they bred and grew strong, rebellion arose of itself.
units.literal: when they multiplied and grew numerous, rebellious intent arose of itself.

units.zh: 以貪悍之性，挾憤怒之情，候隙乘便，輒為橫逆；
units.en: Driven by greedy, violent natures and smoldering rage, they watch for chances and seize them to run riot;
units.literal: with their greedy and fierce nature and their smoldering anger, they watch for openings and seize opportunities, and at once commit outrage;

units.zh: 而居封域之內，無障塞之隔，掩不備之人，收散野之積，故能為禍滋蔓，暴害不測，此必然之勢，已驗之事也。
units.en: and because they live inside the realm itself with no barrier between them, they can strike the unwary and gather grain from the open countryside. Disaster therefore spreads and violence erupts without warning. That is the inevitable course, and history has already proved it.
units.literal: yet they dwell within the sealed domain with no barrier between them, falling upon the unprepared and gathering stores scattered in the countryside—thus calamity can spread and sudden violence burst forth. This is the inevitable tendency, a matter already proved by experience.

units.zh: 當今之宜，宜及兵威方盛，眾事未罷，徙馮翊、北地、新平、安定界內諸羌，著先零、罕幵、析支之地，徙撫風、始平、京兆之氐，出還隴右，著陰平、武都之界，廩其道路之糧，令足自致，各附本種，反其舊土，使屬國、撫夷就安集之。
units.en: The right move now, while our armies are still strong and the campaign not yet wound down, is to move every Qiang within Fufeng, Beidi, Xinping, and Anding back to the territories of Xianling, Hanqian, and Qizhi; to send the Di of Fufeng, Shiping, and Jingzhao out again to Longyou and resettle them on the Yinping and Wudu frontier; to provision their routes so they can travel under their own power, rejoin their clans, and return to their old lands, with the Dependent States and Pacification offices there to receive and settle them.
units.literal: The proper policy for today is, while military might is still at its height and the multitude of affairs is not yet concluded, to relocate all Qiang within the borders of Fufeng, Beidi, Xinping, and Anding to the lands of Xianling, Hanqian, and Qizhi; to move the Di of Fufeng, Shiping, and Jingzhao back out to Longyou and settle them on the borders of Yinping and Wudu; to granary grain for the road so that they may reach their destinations, each attaching to its native clan and returning to its former soil, and to have the Dependent States and Pacification offices receive and settle them.

units.zh: 戎、晉不雜，並得其所，縱有猾夏之心，風塵之警，則絕遠中國，隔閡山河，雖為寇暴，所害不廣矣。
units.en: Rong and Jin would no longer be intermingled, and each people would have its proper place. Even if they still meant to harm the Chinese or war broke out, they would be far from the heartland, cut off by mountains and rivers. They might raid, but the damage would stay limited.
units.literal: Rong and Jin would not be intermixed, and each would obtain its proper place; even if they harbored a mind to harm Xia or alarms of war arose, they would be utterly distant from China, separated by mountains and rivers—though they might raid and plunder, the harm would not be widespread.

units.zh: 難者曰：氐寇新平，關中饑疫，百姓悉苦，咸望寧息；
units.en: A critic objected: The Di rebellion has only just been put down. Guanzhong is stricken with famine and plague. The people are exhausted and crave only peace;
units.literal: An objector said: The Di rebels have only just been pacified; Guanzhong suffers famine and pestilence; the common people are all in distress and long only for rest;

units.zh: 而欲使疲悴之眾，徒自猜之寇，恐勢盡力屈，緒業不卒，前害未及弭而後變復橫出矣。
units.en: yet you would make this worn-out population move a people who already suspect you. Strength may fail, the work may never finish, the first disaster not yet healed before a second erupts.
units.literal: yet you wish to make this weary multitude move a foe that already mistrusts itself—we fear strength will be spent and effort exhausted, the undertaking left unfinished, the former harm not yet quelled when a new disaster breaks out again.

units.zh: 答曰：子以今者群氐為尚挾餘資，悔惡反善，懷我德惠而來柔附乎？
units.en: He answered: Do you imagine today's Di still have reserves of strength, have repented and turned good, and submit out of gratitude for our kindness?
units.literal: The reply was: Do you suppose that today's Di hosts still hold surplus strength, repent of evil and turn to goodness, and come to gentle submission cherishing our virtue and kindness?

units.zh: 將勢窮道盡，智力俱困，懼我兵誅以至於此乎？
units.en: Or is it that their power is spent, their options gone, their wits and strength exhausted, and they bow only because they fear our arms?
units.literal: Or is it that their power is exhausted and their way blocked, wit and strength alike trapped, and they have come to this point because they fear our armies' punishment?

units.zh: 曰：無有餘力，勢窮道盡故也。
units.en: The answer is clear: they have no surplus strength left; their power is spent and their way blocked.
units.literal: The answer: They have no surplus strength; their power is exhausted and their way blocked.

units.zh: 然則我能制其短長之命，而令其進退由己矣。
units.en: If that is so, we can command the length of their lives and decide when they advance or retreat.
units.literal: If so, then we can control the span of their lives and make their coming and going depend on ourselves.

units.zh: 夫樂其業者不易事，安其居者無遷志。
units.en: Those content with their trade do not lightly change it; those settled in their homes have no wish to leave.
units.literal: Those who delight in their occupation do not easily change their work; those secure in their dwelling have no mind to move.

units.zh: 方其自疑危懼，畏怖促遽，故可制以兵威，使之左右無違也，迨其死亡流散，離逖未鳩，與關中之人，戶皆為仇，故可遐遷遠處，令其心不懷土也。
units.en: While they are still uneasy, afraid, and desperate, military force can compel them to obey without resistance. Once they have been broken, scattered, and estranged, every household in Guanzhong their enemy, they can be sent far away so their hearts no longer cling to the land.
units.literal: While they are still suspicious, fearful, and hurried in dread, they can be controlled by military might and made to obey in every direction without defiance. Once they have died off and scattered, estranged and not yet gathered, every household at odds with the people of Guanzhong, they can be moved far away so that their hearts no longer cling to the soil.

units.zh: 夫聖賢之謀事也，為之於未有，治之於未亂，道不著而平，德不顯而成。
units.en: Sages plan before trouble exists and govern before chaos breaks out. Peace comes without displaying the Way; success comes without parading virtue.
units.literal: When sages and worthies plan affairs, they act before anything exists and govern before disorder arises; the Way need not be displayed to bring peace, virtue need not be shown to achieve success.

units.zh: 其次則能轉禍為福，因敗為攻，值困必濟，遇否能通。
units.en: The next best can turn disaster into blessing, build victory out of defeat, rescue the desperate, and find a way through obstruction.
units.literal: The next best can turn calamity into blessing, use defeat as the basis for attack, rescue when caught in hardship, and find passage when blocked.

units.zh: 今子遭敝事之終而不圖更制之始，愛易轍之勤而遵覆車之軌，何哉！
units.en: Yet you stand at the end of a ruined policy and refuse to plan a new beginning. You shrink from the trouble of changing course yet follow the rut of the overturned cart. Why?
units.literal: Now you meet the end of a ruined affair yet do not plan the beginning of a new order; you cherish the toil of changing course yet follow the track of an overturned cart—why!

units.zh: 且關中之人百餘萬口，率其少多，戎、狄居半，處之與遷，必須口實。
units.en: Besides, Guanzhong holds more than a million people, and by rough count the Rong and Di are half of them. Whether they stay or go, every mouth must be fed.
units.literal: Moreover, the people of Guanzhong number more than a million; by rough proportion the Rong and Di make up half. Whether they stay or move, mouths must be fed.

units.zh: 若有窮乏，糝粒不繼者，故當傾關中之谷，以全其生生之計，必無擠於溝壑而不為侵掠之害也。
units.en: If any lack food and cannot even get coarse grain, Guanzhong's stores should be opened to keep them alive, so none are pushed into desperation and turn to plunder.
units.literal: If any are destitute and cannot obtain even coarse grain, the granaries of Guanzhong should be opened to preserve their means of life, so that none are driven into ditches and gullies and then turn to raiding.

units.zh: 今我遷之，傳食而至，附其種疾族，自使相贍，而秦地之人得其半谷，此為濟行者以廩糧，遺居者以積倉，寬關中之逼，去盜賊之原，除旦夕之損，建終年之益。
units.en: Move them now, provision the road until they arrive, let them rejoin their clans and support one another, and the people of Qin will recover half their grain. Travelers gain rations on the march, those who stay keep fuller stores, Guanzhong's crowding eases, the root of banditry is cut, today's losses end, and a benefit is secured for years ahead.
units.literal: If we relocate them now, relaying food until they arrive, letting them attach to their clans and kin so that they support one another, the people of Qin territory would regain half their grain. This supplies travelers with granary grain, leaves those who remain with stored surplus, eases Guanzhong's pressure, removes the source of banditry, ends the damage of the moment, and establishes benefit for years to come.

units.zh: 若憚暫舉之小勞而忘永逸之弘策，惜日月之煩苦而遺累世之寇敵，非所謂能創業垂統，謀及子孫者也。
units.en: To shrink from brief hardship and forget a policy of lasting peace, to spare a few months of trouble and leave enemies to posterity—that is not how one founds an enterprise, hands down a legacy, or plans for one's descendants.
units.literal: If one dreads the small labor of a temporary undertaking and forgets the great policy of lasting ease, spares the annoyance of days and months yet bequeaths enemies to successive generations, this is not what is called founding an enterprise and handing down a legacy, planning for one's descendants.

units.zh: 并州之胡，本實匈奴桀惡之寇也，建安中，使右賢王去卑誘質呼廚泉，聽其部落散居六郡。
units.en: The Hu of Bingzhou were originally the most brutal enemies of the Xiongnu. In the Jian'an era the court sent the Right Worthy King Qubie to entice Huchuquan into hostage status and allowed his tribes to scatter across six commanderies.
units.literal: The Hu of Bingzhou were in origin the fierce and wicked foes of the Xiongnu. In the Jian'an era the Right Worthy King Qubie was sent to entice and hold as hostage Huchuquan, and his tribes were allowed to scatter and dwell across six commanderies.

units.zh: 咸熙之際，以一部太強，分為三率，泰始之初，又增為四；
units.en: Under Xianxi one division grew too powerful and was split into three commandants; at the start of Taishi a fourth was added;
units.literal: At the Xianxi transition one division grew too strong and was split into three commandants; at the beginning of Taishi it was increased to four;

units.zh: 於是劉猛內叛，連結外虜，近者郝散之變，發於穀遠。
units.en: then Liu Meng rebelled from within and allied with outside tribes; the recent Hao San uprising began in Guyuan.
units.literal: thereupon Liu Meng rebelled within and linked with outer barbarians; the recent affair of Hao San arose in Guyuan.

units.zh: 今五部之眾，戶至數萬，人口之盛，過於西戎；
units.en: Today the five divisions count tens of thousands of households, their population greater than that of the western Rong;
units.literal: Today the masses of the five divisions number households in the tens of thousands; their population exceeds that of the western Rong;

units.zh: 其天性驍勇，弓馬便利，倍於氐、羌。
units.en: by nature they are fierce horsemen, doubly dangerous compared with the Di and Qiang.
units.literal: by nature they are fierce and brave, skilled with bow and horse, twice as formidable as the Di and Qiang.

units.zh: 若有不虞風塵之慮，則并州之域可為寒心。
units.en: Should war break out unexpectedly, Bingzhou would be grounds for grave alarm.
units.literal: If unforeseen alarms of war should arise, the territory of Bingzhou would be cause for dread.

units.zh: 正始中，毌丘儉討句驪，徙其餘種於滎陽。
units.en: In the Zhengshi era Guanqiu Jian attacked Goguryeo and moved the survivors to Xingyang.
units.literal: In the Zhengshi era Guanqiu Jian campaigned against Goguryeo and relocated the remnant tribes to Xingyang.

units.zh: 始徙之時，戶落百數；
units.en: At first only a few hundred households were moved;
units.literal: At the time of the first relocation there were only a few hundred households;

units.zh: 子孫孳息，今以千計；
units.en: their descendants have multiplied until they number in the thousands;
units.literal: their descendants multiplied, and today they number in the thousands;

units.zh: 數世之後，必至殷熾。
units.en: and after a few more generations they will surely grow overwhelming.
units.literal: after several generations they will surely grow abundant and powerful.

units.zh: 今百姓失職，猶或亡叛，犬馬肥充，則有噬嚙，況於夷、狄，能不為變！
units.en: Even Chinese who lose their livelihood sometimes flee and rebel. Well-fed dogs and horses will bite. How much more will the Yi and Di refuse to turn violent!
units.literal: Today when the common people lose their livelihood they still sometimes flee and rebel; when dogs and horses are fat and full they will bite—how much more the Yi and Di: can they fail to change!

units.zh: 但顧其微弱，勢力不逮耳。
units.en: Only their present weakness keeps their power from matching their intent.
units.literal: Only consider that they are still weak and their power does not yet reach that far.

units.zh: 夫為邦者，憂不在寡而在不安，以四海之廣，士民之富，豈須夷虜在內然後取足哉！
units.en: A ruler's worry is not scarcity but disorder. With the empire so vast and its people so numerous, must we keep barbarians inside our borders before we have enough!
units.literal: For one who governs a state, the worry lies not in fewness but in unrest. With the four seas so vast and scholars and commoners so abundant, must one rely on barbarians within the realm before having enough!

units.zh: 此等皆可申諭發遣，還其本域，慰彼羈旅懷土之思，釋我華夏纖介之憂，惠此中國，以綏四方，德施永世，於計為長也！」
units.en: All of them can be instructed and sent home to their own lands, easing their longing as strangers abroad, lifting the slightest anxiety from the Chinese heartland, benefiting the central realm and pacifying the four quarters. A policy whose virtue would last for ages—that is the far-sighted course!"
units.literal: All such peoples can be clearly instructed and sent away, returned to their native domains, comforting their longing as sojourners for home, releasing our Huaxia from the slightest worry, benefiting this central state and pacifying the four quarters—virtue extending through ages; in planning this is the long view!"

units.zh: 朝廷不能用。
units.en: The court did not adopt his proposal.
units.literal: The court could not adopt it.

units.zh: 散騎常侍賈謐侍講東宮，對太子倨傲，成都王穎見而叱之；
units.en: Jia Mi, Regular Attendant Within the Encampment, lectured in the Eastern Palace and treated the heir apparent with insolence. Sima Ying, Prince of Chengdu, witnessed it and rebuked him;
units.literal: Jia Mi, Regular Attendant Within the Encampment, lectured in the Eastern Palace and was arrogant toward the Heir Apparent; the Prince of Chengdu, Sima Ying, saw it and rebuked him;

units.zh: 謐怒，言於賈后，出穎為平北將軍，鎮鄴。
units.en: Furious, Mi complained to Empress Jia, who had Ying transferred out as General Who Pacifies the North and posted to Ye.
units.literal: Mi grew angry and spoke to Empress Jia, who sent Ying out as General Who Pacifies the North, stationed at Ye.

units.zh: 征梁王肜為大將軍、錄尚書事；
units.en: Sima Rong, Prince of Liang, was summoned to serve as Grand General and Recorder of the Masters of Writing;
units.literal: The Prince of Liang, Sima Rong, was summoned as Grand General and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing;

units.zh: 以河間王顒為鎮西將軍，鎮關中。
units.en: and Sima Yong, Prince of Hejian, was appointed General Who Guards the West to hold Guanzhong.
units.literal: the Prince of Hejian, Sima Yong, was made General Who Guards the West and stationed in Guanzhong.

units.zh: 初，武帝作石函之制，非至親不得鎮關中；
units.en: Earlier Emperor Wu had decreed in the stone casket that only the closest imperial kin might garrison Guanzhong;
units.literal: Earlier Emperor Wu had established the stone-casket rule: none but the closest kin might garrison Guanzhong;

units.zh: 顒輕財愛士，朝廷以為賢，故用之。
units.en: but Yong was generous and cultivated men of talent, so the court considered him worthy and appointed him anyway.
units.literal: Yong was generous with wealth and cherished scholars; the court regarded him as worthy and therefore employed him.

units.zh: 夏，六月，戊戌，高密文獻王泰薨。
units.en: In summer, the sixth month, on the day wuxu, Sima Tai, the Cultured and Sacrificial King of Gaomi, died.
units.literal: In summer, the sixth month, on the day wuxu, the Cultured and Sacrificial King of Gaomi, Sima Tai, died.

units.zh: 賈后淫虐日甚，私於太醫令程據等；
units.en: Empress Jia's debauchery and cruelty grew worse by the day. She took Cheng Ju, Director of the Imperial Physicians, and others as private lovers;
units.literal: Empress Jia's debauchery and cruelty grew daily worse; she took private relations with the Director of the Imperial Physicians, Cheng Ju, and others;

units.zh: 又以簏箱載道上年少入宮，復恐其漏洩，往往殺之。
units.en: and she had young men smuggled into the palace in bamboo crates. Fearing exposure, she often had them killed afterward.
units.literal: she also used bamboo cases to bring in young men from the roads to the palace, and fearing leaks often killed them.

units.zh: 賈模恐禍及己，甚憂之。
units.en: Jia Mo feared the scandal would engulf him and was deeply alarmed.
units.literal: Jia Mo feared disaster would reach him and was deeply troubled.

units.zh: 裴頠與模及張華議廢后，更立謝淑妃。
units.en: Pei Wei discussed with Mo and Zhang Hua deposing the empress and elevating Lady Xie, the Pure Consort, in her stead.
units.literal: Pei Wei discussed with Mo and Zhang Hua deposing the empress and installing Lady Xie, the Pure Consort, in her place.

units.zh: 模、華皆曰：「主上自無廢黜之意，而吾等專行之，倘上心不以為然，將若之何！
units.en: Mo and Hua both objected: "The emperor himself has no wish to depose her. If we act on our own and he disapproves, what then?
units.literal: Mo and Hua both said: "Our lord himself has no intent to depose her; if we act on our own authority and his heart does not approve, what then shall we do!

units.zh: 且諸王方強，朋黨各異，恐一旦禍起，身死國危，無益社稷。」
units.en: Besides, the princes are strong and their factions divided. If trouble erupts, we may die and the realm fall into peril, with no gain for the state."
units.literal: Moreover the princes are now strong and their factions differ; we fear that if disaster should suddenly arise, we would die and the state be endangered, with no benefit to the altars of soil and grain."

units.zh: 頠曰：「誠如公言。
units.en: Pei replied: "You are right.
units.literal: Pei said: "It is indeed as you say.

units.zh: 然中宮逞其昏虐，亂可立待也。」
units.en: Yet the empress indulges her cruelty and folly. Chaos may come at any moment."
units.literal: Yet the central palace indulges its benighted cruelty; disorder may be awaited at once."

units.zh: 華曰：「卿二人於中宮皆親戚，言或見信，宜數為陳禍福之戒，庶無大悖，則天下尚未至於亂，吾曹得以估游卒歲而已。」
units.en: Zhang Hua said: "You are both related to the empress and may be heard. Warn her often of the consequences. If she avoids the worst excesses, the realm may yet hold together and we can live out our days in peace."
units.literal: Hua said: "You two are both kin to the central palace; your words may win belief. You ought often to set forth warnings of fortune and calamity, so that with luck there will be no great outrage; then the realm may not yet come to disorder, and we may idle through the year as merchants do."

units.zh: 頠旦夕說其從母廣城君，令戒諭賈后以親厚太子，賈模亦數為后言禍福；
units.en: Pei pressed his aunt, the Lady of Guangcheng, day and night to warn Empress Jia to treat the heir apparent kindly. Jia Mo likewise urged the empress repeatedly about the risks she was courting;
units.literal: Pei day and night urged his mother's younger sister, the Lady of Guangcheng, to admonish Empress Jia to treat the Heir Apparent with affection; Jia Mo also repeatedly spoke to the empress of fortune and calamity;

units.zh: 后不能用，反以模為毀己而疏之；
units.en: but she would not listen. She took Mo for a slanderer and estranged herself from him;
units.literal: the empress would not heed them and instead, taking Mo for one who slandered her, kept him at a distance;

units.zh: 模不得志，憂憤而卒。
units.en: and Mo, frustrated and despairing, died of grief.
units.literal: Mo, unable to achieve his aim, died of grief and anger.

units.zh: 秋，八月，以裴頠為尚書僕射。
units.en: In autumn, the eighth month, Pei Wei was appointed Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
units.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, Pei Wei was made Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

units.zh: 頠雖賈后親屬，然雅望素隆，四海唯恐其不居權位，尋詔頠專任門下事，頠上表固辭，以「賈模適亡，復以臣代之，崇外戚之望，彰偏私之舉，為聖朝累。」
units.en: Though Pei was related to Empress Jia, his reputation was so high that the empire wished only that he take office. Soon he was ordered to handle Gate Affairs exclusively. He memorialized to refuse, writing: "Jia Mo has just died and I am put in his place. That elevates the empress's kin, displays favoritism, and burdens the court."
units.literal: Though Pei was kin to Empress Jia, his refined reputation had long been lofty and all within the four seas feared only that he might not hold power; soon an edict made Pei solely responsible for Gate Affairs. Pei submitted a memorial firmly declining, saying: "Jia Mo has just died, and your servant is again put in his place—exalting the hopes of the empress's kin, displaying a partial favoritism, and becoming a burden to the sagely court."

units.zh: 不聽。
units.en: The emperor would not accept his resignation.
units.literal: The emperor would not heed him.

units.zh: 或謂頠曰：「君可以言，當盡言於中宮；
units.en: Someone advised Pei: "If you have influence, speak plainly to the empress;
units.literal: Someone said to Pei: "If you may speak, you ought to speak fully to the central palace;

units.zh: 言而不從，當遠引而去。
units.en: and if she will not listen, withdraw from office.
units.literal: if you speak and are not obeyed, you ought to withdraw far away.

units.zh: 倘二者不立，雖有十表，難以免矣。」
units.en: If you do neither, ten memorials will not save you."
units.literal: If neither course is established, though you submit ten memorials, it will be hard to escape harm."

units.zh: 頠慨然久之，竟不能從。
units.en: Pei sighed for a long time but could not bring himself to follow that counsel.
units.literal: Pei sighed deeply for a long while but in the end could not follow the advice.

units.zh: 帝為人戇騃，嘗在華林園聞蝦蟆，謂左右曰：「此鳴者，為官乎，為私乎？」
units.en: The emperor was dull-witted by nature. Once in the Hualin Garden he heard frogs croaking and asked his attendants: "Are those creatures croaking for the state or for themselves?"
units.literal: The emperor was by nature dull and foolish. Once in the Hualin Garden he heard frogs and said to those at his side: "These that croak—do they croak for office or for private gain?"

units.zh: 時天下荒饉，百姓餓死，帝聞之，曰：「何不食肉糜？」
units.en: Famine ravaged the land and people were starving to death. When he heard of it he said: "Why do they not eat meat porridge?"
units.literal: At that time the realm suffered famine and the common people starved to death. When the emperor heard of it he said: "Why do they not eat meat porridge?"

units.zh: 由是權在群下，政出多門，勢位之家，更相薦托，有如互市。
units.en: Power therefore rested with his ministers. Policy issued from many quarters. Powerful families traded favors and appointments like merchants in a market.
units.literal: From this power lay with the multitude below; government issued from many gates; powerful families recommended and entrusted posts to one another like a mutual marketplace.

units.zh: 賈、郭恣橫，貨賂公行。
units.en: The Jia and Guo factions ruled without restraint, and bribery flourished openly.
units.literal: The Jia and Guo clans acted with unbridled license; bribes walked openly in public.

units.zh: 南陽魯褒作《錢神論》以譏之曰：「錢之為體，有乾坤之象，親之如兄，字曰孔方。
units.en: Lu Bao of Nanyang wrote the "Discourse on the God of Money" to satirize the age, saying: "Money embodies heaven and earth. Men treat it like an elder brother and call it Kongfang.
units.literal: Lu Bao of Nanyang composed the "Discourse on the God of Money" to satirize them, saying: "Money as a substance bears the image of heaven and earth; one treats it as an elder brother and styles it Kongfang.

units.zh: 無德而尊，無勢而熱，排金門，入紫闥。
units.en: Without virtue it is honored; without rank it is courted. It pushes through golden gates and enters the purple chambers of power.
units.literal: Without virtue it is honored; without power it is sought; it pushes through the golden gate and enters the purple portal.

units.zh: 危可使安，死可使活，貴可使賤，生可使殺。
units.en: It can turn danger into safety, death into life, honor into shame, and the living into the dead.
units.literal: Danger it can make safe; death it can make live; the noble it can make base; the living it can make dead.

units.zh: 是故忿爭非錢不勝，幽滯非錢不撥，怨仇非錢不解，令聞非錢不發。
units.en: Angry disputes are not won without it. The imprisoned are not freed without it. Feuds are not settled without it. Reputation is not made without it.
units.literal: Therefore angry disputes are not won without money; the obscure and detained are not released without money; enmity and grievance are not resolved without money; good repute is not spread without money.

units.zh: 洛中朱衣、當塗之士，愛我家兄，皆無已已，執我之手，抱我終始，凡今之人，惟錢而已！」
units.en: The grandees of Luoyang and those who hold power love our elder brother without end, seize my hand and cling to me forever. For the men of today, only money matters!"
units.literal: The scarlet-clad in Luoyang and those who hold the road all love our elder brother without end, grasp my hand and embrace me to the finish—of all people today, only money matters!"

units.zh: 又，朝臣務以苛察相高，每有疑議，群下各立私意，刑法不壹，獄訟繁滋。
units.en: Meanwhile officials competed in harsh scrutiny. Whenever a case was doubtful, each faction pressed its own view. The law lost uniformity and lawsuits multiplied.
units.literal: Moreover the court ministers strove to outdo one another in harsh scrutiny; whenever there was a doubtful case the subordinates each held a private opinion; penal law was not uniform and lawsuits multiplied.

units.zh: 裴頠上表曰：「先王刑賞相稱，輕重無二，故下聽有常，群吏安業。
units.en: Pei Wei memorialized: "The former kings matched punishment to offense and reward to merit, with no arbitrary doubling of severity. Subordinates then knew what to expect and officials pursued their duties in peace.
units.literal: Pei Wei submitted a memorial saying: "The former kings made punishment and reward correspond, with no doubling of light and heavy; therefore those below heard with constancy and the host of officials rested secure in their duties.

units.zh: 去元康四年大風，廟闕屋瓦有數枚傾落，免太常荀寓；
units.en: In the fourth year of Yuankang a great wind blew several tiles from the ancestral temple gate-towers, and Minister of Ceremonies Xun Yu was dismissed;
units.literal: In the fourth year of Yuankang past there was a great wind; several roof-tiles of the ancestral temple gate-towers fell, and the Minister of Ceremonies Xun Yu was dismissed;

units.zh: 事輕責重，有違常典。
units.en: a light offense punished with excessive severity, contrary to precedent.
units.literal: the affair was light but the responsibility heavy, contrary to the regular statutes.

units.zh: 五年二月有大風，蘭台主者懲懼前事，求索阿棟之間，得瓦小邪十五處，遂禁止太常，復興刑獄。
units.en: In the second month of the fifth year another great wind blew. The chief of the Orchid Terrace, dreading a repeat of the earlier scandal, searched the side beams and found fifteen slightly misaligned tiles. He had the Minister of Ceremonies detained and criminal prosecutions revived.
units.literal: In the second month of the fifth year there was again a great wind; the chief of the Orchid Terrace, fearing the former affair, searched between the side beams and found fifteen places where tiles were slightly askew; he thereupon placed the Minister of Ceremonies under detention and revived criminal prosecutions.

units.zh: 今年八月，陵上荊一枝圍七寸二分者被斫；
units.en: In the eighth month of this year a thorn branch seven inches and two tenths around on the imperial mound was cut down;
units.literal: In the eighth month of this year, on the imperial mound a branch of thorn with a circumference of seven inches and two tenths was cut down;

units.zh: 司徒、太常奔走道路，雖知事小，而按劾難測，騷擾驅馳，各競免負，於今太常禁止未解。
units.en: the Minister over the Masses and the Minister of Ceremonies raced about in panic. Though the offense was trivial, no one could predict how prosecution would fall. Officials scrambled to escape blame, and the Minister of Ceremonies remains under detention to this day.
units.literal: the Minister over the Masses and the Minister of Ceremonies rushed along the roads; though they knew the matter was small, prosecution was hard to foresee, and with disturbance and hurried driving each strove to escape blame—down to today the Minister of Ceremonies' detention has not been lifted.

units.zh: 夫刑書之文有限而舛違之故無方，故有臨時議處之制，誠不能皆得循常也。
units.en: Penal statutes are finite, but the causes of violation are endless. Hence there is provision for ad hoc deliberation, and not every case can follow routine precedent.
units.literal: The text of penal statutes is limited while the causes of violation are boundless; therefore there is a system of ad hoc deliberation and disposition, and truly one cannot in every case follow the regular rule.

units.zh: 至於此等，皆為過當，恐奸吏因緣，得為淺深也。」
units.en: Cases like these, however, go too far. I fear corrupt clerks will seize the chance to twist punishments to their own ends."
units.literal: As for cases such as these, all are excessive; I fear corrupt clerks will seize the opportunity to make punishment light or heavy at will."

units.zh: 既而曲議猶不止，三公尚書劉頌復上疏曰：「自近世以來，法漸多門，令甚不一，吏不知所守，下不知所避，奸偽者因以售其情，居上者難以檢其下，事同議異，獄犴不平。
units.en: Yet twisted legal debate continued. Liu Song, Master of Writing to the Three Excellencies, memorialized again: "In recent times laws have multiplied and ordinances conflict. Officials no longer know what to enforce; commoners no longer know what to avoid. Fraud flourishes, superiors cannot control subordinates, identical cases yield different rulings, and justice in the prisons is uneven.
units.literal: Yet twisted deliberation still did not cease. Liu Song, the Three Excellencies' Master of Writing, again submitted a memorial saying: "Since recent times the law has gradually multiplied its gates and ordinances are very inconsistent; clerks do not know what to uphold, the people below do not know what to avoid; the deceitful thereby sell their inclinations, those above find it hard to inspect those below, the same affair receives different deliberations, and the prisons are not fair.

units.zh: 夫君臣之分，各有所司。
units.en: Ruler and minister each have their proper sphere.
units.literal: The distinction between ruler and minister has its respective duties for each.

units.zh: 法欲必奉，故令主者守文；
units.en: Because the law must be obeyed, the presiding officer holds to the statute;
units.literal: The law must be surely obeyed, therefore the presiding officer is made to hold to the text;

units.zh: 理有窮塞，故使大臣釋滯；
units.en: because principle can reach an impasse, great ministers resolve deadlocks;
units.literal: principle has its impasses, therefore great ministers are made to release obstructions;

units.zh: 事有時宜，故人主權斷。
units.en: and because affairs have their timely demands, the sovereign holds discretionary power.
units.literal: affairs have their timely fitness, therefore the sovereign holds discretionary judgment.

units.zh: 主者守文，若釋之執犯蹕之平也；
units.en: The presiding officer who holds to the text is like Zhang Shizhi insisting on the law when the emperor's progress was violated;
units.literal: The presiding officer holding to the text is like Zhang Shizhi's upholding the law on violating the imperial progress;

units.zh: 大臣釋滯，若公孫弘斷郭解之獄也；
units.en: the great minister who resolves deadlock is like Gongsun Hong judging the case of Guo Jie;
units.literal: the great minister releasing obstruction is like Gongsun Hong's deciding the case of Guo Jie;

units.zh: 人主權斷，若漢祖戮丁公之為也。
units.en: the sovereign's discretionary act is like Gaozu of Han executing Lord Ding.
units.literal: the sovereign's discretionary judgment is like Han's Founder's execution of Lord Ding.

units.zh: 天下萬事，自非此類，不得出意妄議，皆以律令從事；
units.en: For all other affairs under heaven, unless they fall into these categories, no one may debate at will. All must proceed by statute and ordinance;
units.literal: For the myriad affairs under heaven, unless they fall into these categories, one may not venture opinion and reckless debate—all must be handled according to statutes and ordinances;

units.zh: 然後法信於下，人聽不惑，吏不容奸，可以言政矣。」
units.en: then the law will be trusted below, the people will not be confused, clerks will have no room for fraud, and government may be called sound."
units.literal: then the law will be trusted below, the people's hearing will not be confused, clerks will not harbor deceit, and one may speak of good government."

units.zh: 乃下詔：「郎、令史復出法駁案者，隨事以聞。」
units.en: An edict followed: "When gentlemen and clerks again raise statutory objections to cases, report each matter as it arises."
units.literal: An edict was then issued: "When gentlemen and clerks again produce legal rebuttals of cases, report the matter according to circumstances."

units.zh: 然亦不能革也。
units.en: Yet the abuse could not be reformed.
units.literal: Yet the practice still could not be reformed.

units.zh: 頌遷吏部尚書，建九班之制，欲令百官居職希遷，考課能否，明其賞罰。
units.en: Song was promoted to Director of Personnel and created a nine-rank system, hoping to make officials aspire to advancement through assessed merit and clear rewards and punishments.
units.literal: Song was transferred to Director of the Masters of Writing for Personnel and established a system of nine ranks, wishing to make the hundred officials in office hope for promotion, examine and assess ability, and clarify rewards and punishments.

units.zh: 賈、郭用權，仕者欲速，事竟不行。
units.en: But the Jia and Guo factions held power, office-seekers wanted quick advancement, and the reform never took effect.
units.literal: The Jia and Guo factions wielded power; those seeking office wanted speed, and the matter in the end was not carried out.

units.zh: 裴頠薦平陽韋忠於張華，華辟之，忠辭疾不起。
units.en: Pei Wei recommended Wei Zhong of Pingyang to Zhang Hua. Hua summoned him, but Zhong pleaded illness and refused to serve.
units.literal: Pei Wei recommended Wei Zhong of Pingyang to Zhang Hua; Hua summoned him, but Zhong declined on grounds of illness and did not take office.

units.zh: 人問其故，忠曰：「張茂先華而不實，裴逸民欲而無厭，棄典禮而附賊後，此豈大丈夫之所為哉！
units.en: Asked why, Zhong said: "Zhang Hua is showy but hollow; Pei Wei is grasping and never satisfied. They abandon ritual and cling to the empress's faction. Is that the conduct of a true gentleman?
units.literal: When people asked his reason, Zhong said: "Zhang Maoxian is flowery but not solid; Pei Yimin is covetous and never satisfied. They abandon canonical rites and attach themselves to the empress's faction—is this what a great man should do!

units.zh: 逸民每有心托我，我常恐其溺於深淵而餘波及我，況可褰裳而就之哉！」
units.en: Wei keeps trying to draw me in. I always fear that if he falls into the abyss the splash will reach me. How could I wade in after him!"
units.literal: Yimin often wishes to entrust affairs to me; I constantly fear that if he falls into the deep abyss the dregs will splash upon me—how much less could I lift my robe and go to him!"

units.zh: 關內侯敦煌索靖，知天下將亂，指洛陽宮門銅駝歎曰：「會見汝在荊棘中耳！」
units.en: Suo Jing of Dunhuang, Marquis within the Passes, foresaw that the realm would soon fall into chaos. Pointing at the bronze camel by the Luoyang palace gate, he sighed: "I shall yet see you standing among thorns and brambles!"
units.literal: Suo Jing of Dunhuang, Marquis within the Passes, knowing the realm would soon fall into disorder, pointed at the bronze camel at the Luoyang palace gate and sighed: "I shall yet see you amid thorns and brambles!"

units.zh: 冬，十一月，甲子朔，日有食之。
units.en: In winter, the eleventh month, on the new moon day jiazi, there was a solar eclipse.
units.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, on the first day jiazi of the month, there was an eclipse of the sun.

units.zh: 初，廣城君郭槐，以賈后無子，常勸后使慈愛太子。
units.en: Earlier Guo Huai, Lady of Guangcheng, because Empress Jia had no son of her own, often urged her to treat the heir apparent kindly.
units.literal: Earlier the Lady of Guangcheng, Guo Huai, because Empress Jia had no son, often urged the empress to treat the Heir Apparent with kindness.

units.zh: 賈謐驕縱，數無禮於太子，廣城君恆切責之。
units.en: Jia Mi was arrogant and repeatedly insulted the heir apparent. The Lady of Guangcheng scolded him harshly again and again.
units.literal: Jia Mi was arrogant and unrestrained, repeatedly disrespectful toward the Heir Apparent; the Lady of Guangcheng constantly rebuked him sharply.

units.zh: 廣城君欲以韓壽女為太子妃，太子亦欲婚韓氏以自固；
units.en: The Lady of Guangcheng wanted Han Shou's daughter as the heir apparent's consort, and the heir apparent likewise hoped to marry into the Han clan to strengthen his position;
units.literal: The Lady of Guangcheng wished to make Han Shou's daughter the Heir Apparent's consort; the Heir Apparent also wished to marry into the Han clan to secure himself;

units.zh: 壽妻賈午及后皆不聽，而為太子聘王衍少女。
units.en: but Han Shou's wife Jia Wu and the empress refused and betrothed the heir apparent to Wang Yan's younger daughter instead.
units.literal: Han Shou's wife Jia Wu and the empress would not agree, and instead betrothed to the Heir Apparent the younger daughter of Wang Yan.

units.zh: 太子聞衍長女美，而后為賈謐聘之，心不能平，頗以為言。
units.en: The heir apparent heard that Yan's elder daughter was beautiful, yet the empress gave her to Jia Mi. He was bitter and complained openly.
units.literal: The Heir Apparent heard that Yan's elder daughter was beautiful, yet the empress betrothed her to Jia Mi; he could not compose his heart and spoke of it with some resentment.

units.zh: 及廣城君病，臨終，執后手，令盡心於太子，言甚切至。
units.en: When the Lady of Guangcheng fell mortally ill, she took the empress's hand at the end and urged her with utmost earnestness to devote herself to the heir apparent.
units.literal: When the Lady of Guangcheng fell ill, at the end she took the empress's hand and ordered her to devote her heart to the Heir Apparent, her words very earnest.

units.zh: 又曰：「趙粲、賈午，必亂汝家事；
units.en: She also said: "Zhao Can and Jia Wu will surely ruin your household.
units.literal: She also said: "Zhao Can and Jia Wu will surely ruin your household affairs;

units.zh: 我死後，勿復聽入。
units.en: After I die, do not let them near you again.
units.literal: after my death, do not again let them enter your counsel.

units.zh: 深記吾言。」
units.en: Remember this well."
units.literal: Remember my words deeply."

units.zh: 后不從，更與粲、午謀害太子。
units.en: The empress ignored her and instead joined Can and Wu in plotting against the heir apparent.
units.literal: The empress did not obey and instead joined with Can and Wu to plot harm to the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 太子幼有令名，及長，不好學，惟與左右嬉戲。
units.en: The heir apparent had a good name as a child, but as he grew he neglected study and played only with his attendants.
units.literal: The Heir Apparent in youth had a fine reputation; when he grew up he did not love learning and only played with those at his side.

units.zh: 賈后復使黃門輩誘之為奢靡威虐，由是名譽浸減，驕慢益彰。
units.en: Empress Jia also set Yellow Gate attendants to lure him into extravagance and cruelty. His reputation faded and his arrogance grew.
units.literal: Empress Jia again had the Yellow Gate attendants entice him into extravagance and cruel arrogance; thereby his reputation gradually declined and his insolence grew more manifest.

units.zh: 或廢朝侍而縱游逸，於宮中為市，使人屠酤，手揣斤兩，輕重不差。
units.en: He sometimes skipped court to roam freely, opened a market inside the palace, had men butcher meat and sell wine, and weighed goods himself without missing by an ounce.
units.literal: He sometimes skipped court attendance to roam in idleness, set up a market within the palace, had men butcher and sell wine, and weighed goods in his own hand without error in light and heavy.

units.zh: 其母，本屠家女也，故太子好之。
units.en: His mother had been a butcher's daughter, which is why he took to such pursuits.
units.literal: His mother had originally been a butcher's daughter, and therefore the Heir Apparent delighted in such things.

units.zh: 東宮月俸錢五十萬，太子常探取二月，用之猶不足。
units.en: The Eastern Palace received five hundred thousand cash a month, yet he often drew two months' stipend at once and still found it insufficient.
units.literal: The Eastern Palace's monthly stipend was five hundred thousand cash; the Heir Apparent often drew two months' worth at once and still found it insufficient.

units.zh: 又令西園賣葵菜、藍子、雞、面等物而收其利。
units.en: He also had the Western Garden sell vegetables, indigo seed, chickens, flour, and other goods for profit.
units.literal: He also ordered the Western Garden to sell mallow, indigo seed, chickens, flour, and the like and collect the profit.

units.zh: 又好陰陽小數，多所拘忌。
units.en: He was also fond of yin-yang lore and petty numerology and observed many taboos.
units.literal: He also loved yin-yang lore and petty numerology and was much bound by taboos.

units.zh: 洗馬江統上書陳五事：「一曰雖有微苦，宜力疾朝侍。
units.en: Jiang Tong, Groom of the Heir Apparent, memorialized with five recommendations: "First, though you are slightly unwell, you should force yourself to attend court.
units.literal: The Groom of the Heir Apparent, Jiang Tong, submitted a memorial setting forth five points: "First, though there is slight illness, you ought to force yourself to attend court.

units.zh: 二曰宜勤見保傅，咨讒善道。
units.en: Second, you should often consult your tutors and seek the path of virtue.
units.literal: Second, you ought diligently to see your tutors and consult them on the good path.

units.zh: 三曰畫室之功，可且減省，後園刻鏤雜作，一皆罷遣。
units.en: Third, cut back on the painting studios and dismiss all carved and inlaid work in the rear garden.
units.literal: Third, the work of the painting studios may for now be reduced; carved and inlaid miscellaneous tasks in the rear garden should all be dismissed.

units.zh: 四曰西園賣葵、藍之屬，虧敗國體，貶損令聞。
units.en: Fourth, selling vegetables and indigo from the Western Garden disgraces the state and harms your reputation.
units.literal: Fourth, selling mallow, indigo, and the like in the Western Garden damages the state's dignity and lowers your fine reputation.

units.zh: 五曰繕牆正瓦，不必拘攣小忌。」
units.en: Fifth, when repairing walls and resetting tiles, you need not be bound by petty taboos."
units.literal: Fifth, when repairing walls and straightening tiles, you need not be bound by petty taboos."

units.zh: 太子皆不從。
units.en: The heir apparent ignored every point.
units.literal: The Heir Apparent would not follow any of them.

units.zh: 中舍人杜錫，恐太子不得安其位，每盡忠諫，勸太子修德業，保令名，言辭懇切。
units.en: Du Xi, Attendant of the Palace Secretariat, fearing the heir apparent might lose his position, repeatedly urged him in loyal remonstrance to cultivate virtue and preserve his good name, his words earnest and forceful.
units.literal: Du Xi, Attendant of the Palace Secretariat, fearing the Heir Apparent could not secure his position, each time offered loyal remonstrance, urging the Heir Apparent to cultivate virtue and preserve his fine name, his words earnest.

units.zh: 太子患之，置針著錫常所坐氈中，刺之流血，錫，預之子也。
units.en: The heir apparent resented this, hid needles in the mat where Xi usually sat, and pricked him until he bled. Xi was the son of Du Yu.
units.literal: The Heir Apparent resented this, placed needles in the mat where Xi usually sat, and pricked him until he bled. Xi was the son of Du Yu.

units.zh: 太子性剛，知賈謐恃中宮驕貴，不能假借之。
units.en: The heir apparent was proud by nature. Knowing Jia Mi relied on the empress's power, he would not indulge him.
units.literal: The Heir Apparent was by nature stern; knowing that Jia Mi relied on the central palace's arrogant eminence, he could not show him favor.

units.zh: 謐時為侍中，至東宮，或捨之，於後庭遊戲。
units.en: Mi was then Attendant of the Yellow Gate. When he visited the Eastern Palace the heir apparent sometimes dismissed him and amused himself in the rear court.
units.literal: Mi was then Attendant of the Yellow Gate; when he came to the Eastern Palace the Heir Apparent sometimes dismissed him and played in the rear court.

units.zh: 詹事裴權諫曰：「謐，后所親暱，一旦交構，則事危矣。」
units.en: Steward Pei Quan warned him: "Mi is the empress's favorite. If you quarrel with him, disaster will follow."
units.literal: The Steward Pei Quan remonstrated: "Mi is one the empress cherishes; if you should clash, the affair would be perilous."

units.zh: 不從。
units.en: He would not listen.
units.literal: He did not heed him.

units.zh: 謐譖太子於后曰：「太子多畜私財以結小人者，為賈氏故也。
units.en: Mi slandered the heir apparent to the empress, saying: "He hoards private wealth to win over petty men because he means to destroy the Jia clan.
units.literal: Mi slandered the Heir Apparent to the empress, saying: "The Heir Apparent amasses private wealth to win over petty men because of the Jia clan.

units.zh: 若宮車晏駕，彼居大位，依楊氏故事，誅臣等，廢后於金墉，如反手耳。
units.en: When the emperor dies and he takes the throne, he will follow the Yang clan precedent, execute us, and imprison you at Jinyong. It will be as easy as turning his hand.
units.literal: If the imperial carriage should halt forever and he take the great position, following the Yang clan precedent he would execute us ministers and depose the empress at Jinyong—it would be like turning the hand.

units.zh: 不如早圖之，更立慈順者，可以自安。」
units.en: Better act early and set up another heir who is mild and obedient. Then we may be safe."
units.literal: Better to plot early, set up another who is kindly and obedient, and thus secure ourselves."

units.zh: 后納其言，乃宣揚太子之短，佈於遠近。
units.en: The empress accepted his counsel and spread the heir apparent's faults far and wide.
units.literal: The empress accepted his words and thereupon spread abroad the Heir Apparent's faults, broadcasting them far and near.

units.zh: 又詐為有娠，內蒿物、產具，取妹夫韓壽子慰祖養之，欲以代太子。
units.en: She also feigned pregnancy, hid birthing supplies inside, took her brother-in-law Han Shou's son Weizu to rear, and planned to replace the heir apparent with him.
units.literal: She also feigned pregnancy, hid artemisia and birthing gear within, took her brother-in-law Han Shou's son Weizu to rear, and intended to replace the Heir Apparent with him.

units.zh: 於時朝野咸知賈后有害太子之意，中護軍趙俊請太子廢后，太子不聽。
units.en: By then everyone knew Empress Jia meant to destroy the heir apparent. Zhao Jun, Central Protector of the Army, urged him to depose her, but he refused.
units.literal: At that time court and commonalty alike knew Empress Jia meant harm to the Heir Apparent; the Central Protector of the Army Zhao Jun asked the Heir Apparent to depose the empress, but the Heir Apparent would not listen.

units.zh: 左衛率東平劉卞，以賈后之謀問張華，華曰：「不聞。」
units.en: Liu Bian of Dongping, Colonel of the Left Guards, asked Zhang Hua about the empress's plot. Hua said, "I have heard nothing."
units.literal: Liu Bian of Dongping, Colonel of the Left Guards, asked Zhang Hua about Empress Jia's plot; Hua said: "I have not heard of it."

units.zh: 卞曰：「卞自須昌小吏，受公成拔以至今日。
units.en: Bian said, "I was only a petty clerk in Xuchang until you raised me to what I am today.
units.literal: Bian said: "Bian rose from a petty clerk in Xuchang through your grace's full promotion to reach today.

units.zh: 士感知己，是以盡言，而公更有疑於卞邪！」
units.en: A gentleman repays his patron with full candor. Do you still doubt me?"
units.literal: A gentleman who knows gratitude to his patron therefore speaks fully—yet does Your Excellency still doubt Bian!"

units.zh: 華曰：「假令有此，君欲如何？」
units.en: Hua asked, "Suppose it were true. What would you do?"
units.literal: Hua said: "Suppose there were such a thing—what would you intend?"

units.zh: 卞曰：「東宮俊乂如林，四率精兵萬人；
units.en: Bian said, "The Eastern Palace has talent in abundance, and the four colonels command ten thousand elite troops.
units.literal: Bian said: "The Eastern Palace has talented men like a forest; the four colonels command elite troops of ten thousand;

units.zh: 公居阿衡之任，若得公命，皇太子因朝入錄尚書事，廢賈后於金墉城，兩黃門力耳。」
units.en: You hold the chief minister's power. With your order the heir apparent could enter court, take charge of the Masters of Writing, and depose Empress Jia at Jinyong. It would take only two Yellow Gate attendants."
units.literal: Your Excellency holds the office of chief minister; if we obtain your command, the Heir Apparent can enter at court to record the Masters of Writing affairs and depose Empress Jia at Jinyong—it is only the strength of two Yellow Gate attendants."

units.zh: 華曰：「今天子當陽，太子，人子也，吾又不受阿衡之命，忽相與行此，是無君父而以不孝示天下也。
units.en: Hua said, "The emperor reigns in his own right. The heir apparent is his son, and I have received no commission as chief minister. To act suddenly in this way would be to cast aside ruler and father and show the world an act of filial impiety.
units.literal: Hua said: "Today the Son of Heaven faces the sun; the Heir Apparent is a human son, and I have not received the chief minister's commission—suddenly to act together in this would be to have no ruler or father and display filial impiety to the realm.

units.zh: 雖能有成，猶不免罪。
units.en: Even if we succeeded, we would still be guilty.
units.literal: Even if we could succeed, we would still not escape guilt.

units.zh: 況權戚滿朝，威柄不一，成可必乎？」
units.en: Besides, powerful kin fill the court and power is divided. Can success be certain?"
units.literal: Moreover the powerful kin fill the court and authority is not unified—can success be certain?"

units.zh: 賈后常使親黨微服聽察於外，頗聞卞言，乃遷卞為雍州刺史；
units.en: Empress Jia often had her kin spy in disguise and learned of Bian's words. She transferred him to Inspector of Yongzhou;
units.literal: Empress Jia often had her kin in plain dress listen and observe outside and heard much of Bian's words; she thereupon transferred Bian to be Inspector of Yongzhou;

units.zh: 卞知言洩，飲藥而死。
units.en: and Bian, knowing his plot had leaked, took poison and died.
units.literal: Bian, knowing his words had leaked, took poison and died.

units.zh: 十二月，太子長子虨病，太子為虨求王爵，不許。
units.en: In the twelfth month the heir apparent's eldest son Sima Bin fell ill. The heir apparent asked that he be made a prince, but the request was denied.
units.literal: In the twelfth month the Heir Apparent's eldest son Sima Bin fell ill; the Heir Apparent sought a princely title for Bin but was not granted it.

units.zh: 虨疾篤，太子為之禱祀求福。
units.en: As Bin grew gravely ill, the heir apparent prayed and offered sacrifices on his behalf.
units.literal: When Bin's illness grew grave, the Heir Apparent prayed and offered sacrifices to seek blessing for him.

units.zh: 賈后聞之，乃詐稱帝不豫，召太子入朝，既至，后不見，置於別室，遣婢陳舞以帝命賜太子酒三升，使盡飲之。
units.en: Empress Jia heard of this and falsely announced that the emperor was ill, summoning the heir apparent to court. When he arrived she refused to see him, placed him in a side room, and sent the maid Chen Wu with the emperor's name to give him three pints of wine and order him to drink it all.
units.literal: When Empress Jia heard of it she falsely announced the emperor was unwell and summoned the Heir Apparent to court; once he arrived the empress did not see him but placed him in a separate room and sent the maid Chen Wu, in the emperor's name, to bestow three pints of wine on the Heir Apparent and order him to drink it all.

units.zh: 太子辭以不能飲三升，舞逼之曰：「不孝邪！
units.en: He declined, saying he could not drink so much. Wu pressed him: "Are you unfilial?
units.literal: The Heir Apparent declined, saying he could not drink three pints; Wu pressed him: "Are you unfilial!

units.zh: 天賜汝酒而不飲，酒中有惡物邪！」
units.en: Heaven grants you wine and you refuse. Do you think it poisoned?"
units.literal: Heaven bestows wine upon you and you will not drink—is there something evil in the wine!"

units.zh: 太子不得已，強飲至盡，遂大醉。
units.en: Unable to refuse further, he drank it all and became thoroughly drunk.
units.literal: The Heir Apparent had no choice, forced himself to drink to the end, and became very drunk.

units.zh: 后使黃門侍朗潘岳作書草，令小婢承福，以紙筆及草，因太子醉，稱詔使書之，文曰：「陛下宜自了，不自了，吾當入了之。
units.en: The empress had Pan Yue, Yellow Gate Attendant, draft a letter and sent the maid Cheng Fu with paper, brush, and draft. While the heir apparent was drunk she claimed an imperial order and made him copy it. The text read: "Your Majesty ought to settle this yourself. If you do not, I shall enter and settle it.
units.literal: The empress had the Yellow Gate Attendant Pan Yue draft a letter, ordered the little maid Cheng Fu to bring paper, brush, and draft; taking advantage of the Heir Apparent's drunkenness she claimed an edict and made him write it. The text read: "Your Majesty ought to settle matters yourself; if you do not settle them, I shall enter and settle them.

units.zh: 中宮又宜速自了，不自了，吾當手了之。
units.en: The empress too ought quickly to settle matters herself. If she does not, I shall settle them with my own hand.
units.literal: The central palace too ought quickly to settle matters herself; if she does not, I shall settle them with my own hand.

units.zh: 並與謝妃共要，刻期兩發，勿疑猶豫，以致後患。
units.en: I have agreed with Consort Xie. We have set a date for both to act. Do not hesitate and bring later trouble.
units.literal: Together with Consort Xie we have agreed; set a date for both to act—do not doubt or hesitate and bring later trouble.

units.zh: 茹毛飲血於三辰之下，皇天許當掃除患害，立道文為王，蔣氏為內主。
units.en: We shall eat raw flesh and drink blood under heaven. August Heaven has promised to sweep away the harm, establish Daowen as king, and make the Jiang clan the inner mistress.
units.literal: Eating raw flesh and drinking blood beneath the three luminaries—August Heaven has promised to sweep away the harm, establish Daowen as king, and make the Jiang clan the inner mistress.

units.zh: 願成，當三牲祠北君。」
units.en: When it succeeds, we shall offer the three sacrificial beasts to the Northern Lord."
units.literal: When the wish is fulfilled, we shall offer the three sacrificial beasts to the Northern Lord."

units.zh: 太子醉迷不覺，遂依而寫之。
units.en: Drunk and unaware, he copied it as dictated.
units.literal: The Heir Apparent, drunk and dazed and unaware, thereupon copied it as given.

units.zh: 其字半不成，后補成之，以呈帝。
units.en: Half the characters were incomplete. The empress finished them and presented the letter to the emperor.
units.literal: Half his characters were incomplete; the empress completed them and presented it to the emperor.

units.zh: 壬戌，帝幸式乾殿，召公卿入，使黃門令董猛以太子書及青紙詔示之曰：「遹書如此，今賜死。」
units.en: On the day renxu the emperor went to the Shiqian Hall and summoned the ministers. Yellow Gate Commandant Dong Meng showed them the heir apparent's letter and a blue-paper edict, saying: "Yu wrote this. He is to die."
units.literal: On the day renxu the emperor visited the Shiqian Hall, summoned the excellencies and ministers in, and had the Yellow Gate Commandant Dong Meng show them the Heir Apparent's letter and the blue-paper edict, saying: "Yu's letter is thus—now grant death."

units.zh: 遍示諸公王，莫有言者。
units.en: He showed it to all the princes and nobles. No one spoke.
units.literal: He showed it to all the princes and lords; none spoke.

units.zh: 張華曰：「此國之大禍，自古以來，常因廢黜正嫡以致喪亂。
units.en: Zhang Hua said, "This is a great calamity for the state. Since antiquity disorder has often followed the deposition of the legitimate heir.
units.literal: Zhang Hua said: "This is a great calamity for the state. Since antiquity disorder has often come from deposing the legitimate heir.

units.zh: 且國家有天下日淺，願陛下詳之！」
units.en: Moreover the dynasty has held the realm only a short time. I beg Your Majesty to consider carefully!"
units.literal: Moreover the state has held the realm but a short time—I beg Your Majesty to consider carefully!"

units.zh: 裴頠以為宜先檢校傳書者，又請比較太子手書，不然，恐有詐妄。
units.en: Pei Wei urged that the messenger be examined first and the handwriting compared with the heir apparent's own script, lest the letter be a forgery.
units.literal: Pei Wei held that one ought first to examine and verify the person who transmitted the letter, and also requested comparison with the Heir Apparent's own handwriting; otherwise he feared there might be fraud.

units.zh: 賈后乃出太子啟事十餘紙，眾人比視，亦無敢言非者。
units.en: Empress Jia then produced more than ten sheets of the heir apparent's memorials. When the assembly compared them, no one dared say they did not match.
units.literal: Empress Jia then produced more than ten sheets of the Heir Apparent's memorials; when the assembly compared them, none dared say they did not match.

units.zh: 賈后使董猛矯以長廣公主辭白帝曰：「事宜速決，而群臣各不同，其不從詔者，宜以軍法從事。」
units.en: Empress Jia had Dong Meng report to the emperor in the name of the Princess of Changguang: "This must be decided at once. The ministers are divided. Those who disobey the edict should be dealt with by military law."
units.literal: Empress Jia had Dong Meng, falsely in the name of the Princess of Changguang, report to the emperor: "The affair ought to be decided quickly, yet the ministers all differ; those who do not follow the edict ought to be handled by military law."

units.zh: 議至日西，不決。
units.en: Debate continued until sunset without resolution.
units.literal: Deliberation continued until the sun was in the west, without decision.

units.zh: 后見華等意堅，懼事變，乃表免太子為庶人，詔許之。
units.en: Seeing Zhang Hua and the others hold firm and fearing the plot might fail, the empress memorialized to depose the heir apparent as a commoner. The edict was approved.
units.literal: The empress, seeing that Hua and the others were firm in intent and fearing the affair might change, submitted a memorial to depose the Heir Apparent as commoner; an edict approved it.

units.zh: 於是使尚書和郁等持節詣東宮，廢太子為庶人，太子改服出，再拜受詔，步出承華門，乘粗犢車，車武公澹以兵仗送太子及妃王氏、三子虨、臧、尚同幽於金墉城。
units.en: He Yu of the Masters of Writing and others were sent with credentials to the Eastern Palace. The heir apparent changed his garments, bowed twice, received the edict, walked out through the Chenghua Gate, and rode a rough ox-cart. Sima Dan, Duke of Dongwu, escorted him with armed guards, together with his consort Lady Wang and his three sons Bin, Zang, and Shang, to confinement at Jinyong.
units.literal: Thereupon He Yu of the Masters of Writing and others were sent with credentials to the Eastern Palace to depose the Heir Apparent as commoner. The Heir Apparent changed his garments and came out, bowed twice and received the edict, walked out through the Chenghua Gate, rode a rough ox-cart, and the Duke of Dongwu, Sima Dan, with arms escorted the Heir Apparent, his consort Lady Wang, and his three sons Bin, Zang, and Shang together to be confined at Jinyong.

units.zh: 王衍自表離婚，許之，妃慟哭而歸。
units.en: Wang Yan memorialized to divorce her, and permission was granted. The consort returned home in bitter tears.
units.literal: Wang Yan himself submitted a memorial requesting divorce; it was granted, and the consort returned home weeping bitterly.

units.zh: 殺太子母謝淑媛及虨母保林蔣俊。
units.en: The heir apparent's mother, Lady Xie the Gracious Lady, and Bin's mother, Jiang Jun, a consort of baolin rank, were executed.
units.literal: The Heir Apparent's mother, the Gracious Lady Xie, and Bin's mother, Jiang Jun, a consort of baolin rank, were killed.

units.zh: 孝惠皇帝上之下永康元年（
units.en: Under Emperor Hui of Jin, Yongkang, year 1 (
units.literal: The lower portion of the first reign of Emperor Xiaohui, first year of Yongkang (

units.zh: 庚申，公元三零零年）
units.en: gengshen, CE 300)
units.literal: gengshen, common era year 300)

units.zh: 春，正月，癸亥朔，赦天下，改元。
units.en: In spring, the first month, on the new moon day guihai, the realm was granted amnesty and the era name was changed.
units.literal: In spring, the first month, on the new moon day guihai, amnesty was granted to the realm and the era name was changed.

units.zh: 西戎校尉司馬閻纘輿棺詣闕上書，以為：「漢戾太子稱兵拒命，言者猶曰罪當笞耳。
units.en: Yan Xun, Major under the Colonel of the Western Rong, came to the palace gate with his coffin on a cart and submitted a memorial, arguing: "When Emperor Wu's heir apparent Liu Ju took up arms in rebellion, critics still said his offense deserved only a beating.
units.literal: Yan Xun, Major of the Colonel of the Western Rong, came to the gate with his coffin on a cart and submitted a memorial, holding: "When the Han Heir Apparent Li raised troops and defied orders, those who spoke still said his crime merited only the bastinado.

units.zh: 今遹受罪之日，不敢失道，猶為輕於戾太子。
units.en: Now Yu stands condemned yet has not strayed from duty; even so his case is still treated more leniently than that of Crown Prince Li.
units.literal: Now on the day Yu received punishment he did not dare stray from the Way, yet this is still lighter than the Heir Apparent Li.

units.zh: 宜重選師傅，先加嚴誨，若不悛改，棄之未晚也。」書奏，不省。
units.en: The court should appoint new tutors and admonish him strictly. If he does not reform, deposing him would not yet be too late." The memorial was submitted, but it was not examined.
units.literal: One ought to choose tutors anew and first apply stern instruction; if he does not repent and reform, to discard him would not be too late." The memorial was submitted, but it was not examined.

units.zh: 纘，圃之孫也。
units.en: Xun was the grandson of Yan Pu.
units.literal: Xun was the grandson of Yan Pu.

units.zh: 賈后使黃門自首欲與太子為逆。
units.en: Empress Jia had a Yellow Gate attendant confess a plot to rebel with the heir apparent.
units.literal: Empress Jia had a Yellow Gate attendant confess that he wished to rebel with the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 詔以黃門首辭班示公卿，遣東武公澹以千兵防衛太子，幽於許昌宮，令持書御史劉振持節守之，詔宮臣不得辭送。
units.en: An edict showed the confession to the ministers, sent Sima Dan, Marquis of Dongwu, with a thousand troops to guard the heir apparent at Xuchang Palace, and ordered Liu Zhen, Attendant Secretary with credentials, to hold him under guard, forbidding palace officials to escort him on departure.
units.literal: An edict displayed the Yellow Gate confessor's testimony to the excellencies and ministers, dispatched the Marquis of Dongwu Sima Dan with a thousand troops to guard the Heir Apparent, confined him at the Xuchang palace, ordered the Attendant Secretary with credentials Liu Zhen to hold him under guard, and decreed that palace officials might not take leave to escort him.

units.zh: 洗馬江統、潘滔、舍人王敦、杜蕤、魯瑤等冒禁至伊水，拜辭涕泣。
units.en: Jiang Tong, Pan Tao, Wang Dun, Du Rui, Lu Yao, and others defied the ban, went to the Yi River, bowed farewell, and wept.
units.literal: The Groom Jiang Tong, Pan Tao, Attendant Wang Dun, Du Rui, Lu Yao, and others braved the prohibition to reach the Yi River, bowed in farewell, and wept.

units.zh: 司隸校尉滿奮收縛統籌送獄。
units.en: Colonel of the Censorate Man Fen arrested Tong and the others and sent them to prison.
units.literal: The Colonel of the Censorate Man Fen arrested and bound Tong and his companions and sent them to prison.

units.zh: 其系河南獄者，樂廣悉解遣之；
units.en: Those held in the Henan prison were all released by Yue Guang;
units.literal: Those held in the Henan prison were all released by Yue Guang;

units.zh: 系洛陽縣獄者，猶未釋。
units.en: those held in the Luoyang county prison were not yet released.
units.literal: those held in the Luoyang county prison were still not released.

units.zh: 都官從事孫琰說賈謐曰：「所以廢徙太子，以其為惡故耳。
units.en: Director of Justice Sun Yan told Jia Mi: "The heir apparent was deposed because he was wicked.
units.literal: Director of Justice Sun Yan said to Jia Mi: "The reason for deposing and relocating the Heir Apparent is that he was wicked.

units.zh: 今宮臣冒罪拜辭，而加以重辟；
units.en: Yet you would punish palace officials who came to bid him farewell;
units.literal: Now palace officials offend the law to bid farewell; yet you add heavy punishment;

units.zh: 流聞四方，乃更彰太子之德也，不如釋之。」
units.en: If word spreads abroad it will only highlight the heir apparent's virtue. Better release them."
units.literal: if this spreads to the four quarters it will only make the Heir Apparent's virtue more manifest—better to release them."

units.zh: 謐乃語洛陽令曹攄使釋之；
units.en: Mi then told Cao Shu, Magistrate of Luoyang, to release them;
units.literal: Mi thereupon told the Magistrate of Luoyang Cao Shu to release them;

units.zh: 廣亦不坐。
units.en: Guang was not punished either.
units.literal: Guang was also not punished.

units.zh: 敦，覽之孫；
units.en: Dun was the grandson of Wang Lan;
units.literal: Dun was the grandson of Wang Lan;

units.zh: 攄，肇之孫也。
units.en: Shu was the grandson of Cao Zhao.
units.literal: Shu was the grandson of Cao Zhao.

units.zh: 太子至許，遺王妃書，自陳誣枉，妃父衍不敢以聞。
units.en: At Xu the heir apparent wrote to his consort proclaiming his innocence; her father Wang Yan did not dare report it.
units.literal: When the Heir Apparent reached Xu he sent a letter to the consort stating his false accusation; the consort's father Yan did not dare report it.

units.zh: 丙子，皇孫虨卒。
units.en: On the day bingzi the imperial grandson Bin died.
units.literal: On the day bingzi the imperial grandson Bin died.

units.zh: 三月，尉氏雨血，妖星見南方，太白晝見，中台星拆。
units.en: In the third month blood rained at Weishi, an ominous star appeared in the south, Venus was seen by day, and the Central Terrace star split.
units.literal: In the third month blood rained at Weishi, an ominous star appeared in the south, the Great White was seen by day, and the Central Terrace star split.

units.zh: 張華少子韙勸華遜位，華不從，曰：「天道幽遠，不如靜以待之。」
units.en: Hua's younger son Wei urged him to resign; Hua refused, saying: "Heaven's way is obscure. Better to wait quietly."
units.literal: Zhang Hua's younger son Wei urged Hua to yield his post; Hua would not, saying: "The Way of Heaven is remote and obscure—better to wait quietly."

units.zh: 太子既廢，眾情憤怒。
units.en: Once the heir apparent was deposed, public anger boiled over.
units.literal: Once the Heir Apparent was deposed, public sentiment was furious.

units.zh: 有衛督司馬雅、常從督許超，皆嘗給事東宮，與殿中郎士猗等謀廢賈后，復太子。
units.en: Sima Ya, Colonel of the Guards, and Xu Chao, Regular Colonel of the Followers, both former Eastern Palace attendants, joined Palace Gentleman Shi Yi and others to plot deposing Empress Jia and restoring the heir apparent.
units.literal: The Colonel of the Guards Sima Ya and the Regular Colonel of the Followers Xu Chao, who had both once served the Eastern Palace, joined the Palace Gentleman Shi Yi and others in plotting to depose Empress Jia and restore the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 以張華、裴頠安常保位，難與行權，右軍將軍趙王倫執兵柄，性貪冒，可假以濟事。
units.en: They judged Zhang Hua and Pei Wei too cautious to act, while Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao, held the armies and was greedy—he could be used.
units.literal: They judged Zhang Hua and Pei Wei content to preserve their posts and hard to move to action, while the General of the Right Army the Prince of Zhao Sima Lun held military power and was greedy—he could be borrowed to accomplish the affair.

units.zh: 乃說孫秀曰：「中宮凶妒無道，與賈謐等共誣廢太子。
units.en: They told Sun Xiu: "The empress is vicious and lawless. With Jia Mi she framed and deposed the heir apparent.
units.literal: They thereupon said to Sun Xiu: "The central palace is fierce, jealous, and without the Way, and together with Jia Mi and others falsely deposed the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 今國無嫡嗣，社稷將危，大臣將起大事，而公名奉事中宮，與賈、郭親善，太子之廢，皆云豫知，一朝事起，禍必相及，何不先謀之乎！」
units.en: The realm lacks a legitimate heir and the altars are endangered. Great ministers will act, yet you serve the empress and are close to the Jia and Guo clans. When the heir apparent fell, men said you knew beforehand. When trouble erupts you will not escape—why not strike first?"
units.literal: Now the state has no legitimate heir and the altars are in peril; the great ministers will raise a great affair, yet you by name attend the central palace and are intimate with the Jia and Guo—when the Heir Apparent was deposed all said you foreknew it. Once trouble rises disaster must reach you—why not plot first!"

units.zh: 秀許諾，言於倫，倫納焉，遂告通事令史張林及省事張衡等，使為內應。
units.en: Xiu agreed and told Lun, who accepted and enlisted Zhang Lin and Zhang Heng as inside agents.
units.literal: Xiu promised and spoke to Lun; Lun accepted, and reported to the clerks Zhang Lin and Zhang Heng among the communications staff to serve as inside agents.

units.zh: 事將起，孫秀言於倫曰：「太子聰明剛猛，若還東宮，必不受制於人。
units.en: Before the coup Sun Xiu told Lun: "The heir apparent is clever and fierce. Restored to the Eastern Palace he will not submit to anyone.
units.literal: As the affair was about to begin, Sun Xiu said to Lun: "The Heir Apparent is intelligent, stern, and fierce; if restored to the Eastern Palace he will surely not be controlled by others.

units.zh: 明公素黨於賈后，道路皆知之，今雖建大功於太子，太子謂公特逼於百姓之望，翻覆以免罪耳，雖含忍宿忿，必不能深德明公，若有瑕釁，猶不免誅。
units.en: You have always sided with the empress—everyone knows it. Even if you now save him, he will think you acted only under public pressure and may turn on you to clear himself. Old grudges will not become deep gratitude; the slightest fault could still cost your life.
units.literal: Your Excellency has always been of the empress's party—the roads all know it. Though you now perform a great service for the Heir Apparent, he will say you acted only under the people's pressure and may turn to escape guilt; though he swallow old resentment he cannot deeply reward you, and if there be a flaw you still cannot escape execution.

units.zh: 不若遷延緩期，賈后必害太子，然後廢賈后，為太子報仇，豈徒免禍而已，乃更可以得志！」
units.en: Delay instead. The empress will kill him. Then depose her and avenge him—not merely escaping harm but winning your ambition!"
units.literal: Better to delay and wait: the empress will surely harm the Heir Apparent; then depose the empress and avenge the Heir Apparent—not only escaping disaster but gaining your ambition!"

units.zh: 倫然之。
units.en: Lun agreed.
units.literal: Lun agreed.

units.zh: 秀因使人行反間，言殿中人欲廢皇后，迎太子。
units.en: Xiu spread disinformation that palace insiders meant to depose the empress and restore the heir apparent.
units.literal: Xiu therefore sent men to spread counter-intelligence, saying those in the palace wished to depose the empress and welcome the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 賈后數遣宮婢微服於民間聽察，聞之甚懼。
units.en: The empress often sent maids in disguise to listen among the people and was terrified.
units.literal: Empress Jia often sent palace maids in plain dress among the people to listen; hearing this she was greatly afraid.

units.zh: 倫、秀因勸謐等早除太子，以絕眾望。
units.en: Lun and Xiu urged Mi and others to kill the heir apparent at once and end public hope.
units.literal: Lun and Xiu therefore urged Mi and the rest to eliminate the Heir Apparent early and cut off public hope.

units.zh: 癸未，賈后使太醫令程據和毒藥。
units.en: On guiwei the empress had Cheng Ju, Director of Imperial Physicians, prepare poison.
units.literal: On the day guiwei Empress Jia had the Director of Imperial Physicians Cheng Ju compound poison.

units.zh: 矯詔使黃門孫慮至許昌毒太子。
units.en: A forged edict sent Sun Lv of the Yellow Gate to Xuchang to poison the heir apparent.
units.literal: A forged edict sent the Yellow Gate Sun Lv to Xuchang to poison the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 太子自廢黜，恐被毒，常自煮食於前；
units.en: Since his deposition he feared poison and often cooked for himself;
units.literal: Since his deposition the Heir Apparent feared poison and often cooked his own food beforehand;

units.zh: 慮以告劉振，振乃徙太子於小坊中，絕其食，宮人猶竊於牆上過食與之。
units.en: Lv told Liu Zhen, who moved him to a small compound and cut off food, though palace women still passed food over the wall.
